authenticity_review: Upon reflection, I must adjust my authenticity score downward. While the Router noted 'moderate compression' (severity 0.4) and texture anomalies, the visual evidence shows more pervasive issues than initially weighted. The shell plates lack the expected granular, calcareous micro-texture; instead, they exhibit a smooth, almost painted quality with repetitive central markings that appear algorithmically stamped rather than biologically grown. The girdle texture, while distinct from the background per the topology audit, lacks the fine leathery/spiny detail described in the taxonomy. These are not just compression artifacts but fundamental textural hallucinations. The perceptual quality auditor's 'moderate compression' verdict likely underestimates the severity of this textural failure, which affects biological realism more than mere image fidelity. I will lower the authenticity score to reflect this compounded textural deficiency.

authenticity_reasoning: The image exhibits significant textural deficiencies beyond simple compression. The shell plates show a waxy, over-smoothed appearance lacking the hard, granular surface of real calcareous valves. The central dark markings are unnaturally uniform and repetitive across plates, indicating generative patterning rather than biological variation. While the topology auditor confirmed good segmentation (mask confidence 0.96), this does not compensate for the internal textural hallucinations. The perceptual quality auditor's 'moderate compression' finding (severity 0.4) captures part of the issue but underweights the biological implausibility of the textures. Combined with the Router's noted edge softness (severity 1), these factors justify a lower authenticity score that reflects both technical and biological realism failures.
